A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LogicXGNN, retaining its central predicate-and-rule framework and five principal benchmarks despite substantial revision and retitling. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original classification and runtime experiments, architecture comparisons, scaffold-shift and node-classification results, rule-stability measurements, and generated graph examples.

after.justification: V3 reports original grounded-fidelity and runtime experiments, scalability results, explanation-utility measurements, tree-depth sensitivity, and grounding case studies.

M1.justification: V3 replaces v2's grounding inputs of central-node features and neighboring predicate frequencies with feature aggregation over ordered automorphism orbits (Definition 3.1 and Algorithm 1). The predicate-selection tree now targets GNN predictions instead of dataset labels. V2's descriptive-rule, connectivity-pattern, and graph-generation procedures are removed, substantially revising the pipeline.

E1.justification: V3 retains the five principal graph-classification datasets and adds Reddit Threads, Twitch Egos, GitHub Stargazers, and a continuous-feature modification of Mutagenicity. It removes HIN, PROTEINS, AIDS, Cora/PubMed node classification, the scaffold-shift scenarios involving BACE/BBBP/SIDER, and graph-generation evaluations. These alter both coverage and task requirements.

E2.justification: GLGExplainer and GraphTrail remain the principal explanation baselines, but the evaluated XGNN generation comparison disappears. V3 Table 13 adds the best GLGExplainer/GraphTrail comparator to the architecture comparison that contained only GNN and LogicXGNN results in v2 Table 11. Both explanation baselines also enter the new comparative stability analysis.

E3.justification: V3 makes class-weighted data-grounded fidelity the primary metric, explicitly penalizing ambiguous rule outputs, and evaluates precision/recall/F1 against GNN predictions. It changes the default architectures for Mutagenicity, NCI1, and IMDB to GCN. New protocols include a 12-hour explainer budget, baseline subgraph matching with per-instance timeouts and exclusions, and controlled explanation complexity for utility comparisons; the 80/20 split remains.

E4.justification: V3 adds tree-depth sensitivity, concept-space versus grounded-fidelity comparisons, quantitative coverage/stability/validity analyses, baseline grounding-error investigations, and a continuous-feature case study. V2's scaffold-shift tests, five-fold clause-overlap study, and clause-frequency histograms are removed. These substantially change the questions investigated beyond aggregate benchmark performance.

E5.justification: Both versions already use three seeds and report values with ± uncertainty. V3 newly clarifies that seeds affect the entire pipeline, including GNN training, while LogicXGNN itself is deterministic. Five-fold clause-overlap reporting is replaced by three-run subgraph-intersection stability; unlike v2, v3 does not explicitly identify its ± quantities as standard deviations.

E6.justification: Numerical and qualitative results are extensively replaced. For example, LogicXGNN's BBBP accuracy is 85.13±2.20% in v2 Table 5 and 78.06±4.28% in v3 Table 9; v3 separately reports 85.32±2.96% grounded fidelity. V3 also reports no learned GLGExplainer rules on BBBP, unlike v2, and adds scalability and utility outcomes. Revised methods and protocols prevent interpreting these as same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: V3 introduces automorphism-orbit definitions, a revised mathematical grounding representation, Theorem D.1 and its proof, and formal definitions of grounded fidelity and utility metrics. Section 3.4 revises hashing complexity from O(|V|) to O(|V|L(ν+ε)) and grounding complexity from O(|V|) to O(|V|²). These are substantive mathematical additions and revisions.

C1.justification: V2 foregrounds functional equivalence to GNNs, classification superiority, chemical knowledge discovery, and controllable graph generation. V3 centers its contributions on identifying unreliable grounding, introducing data-grounded fidelity, and achieving over 20% average fidelity improvement with practical explanation utility and scalability. The functional-equivalence and generative-model contribution claims disappear, while the runtime-speedup claim remains.

C2.justification: V3 replaces much of v2's chemical-mechanism and rule-structured-data interpretation with explanations involving conflicting rules, invalid baseline subgraphs, grounding generalization, and fidelity–complexity tradeoffs. It adds reasons for avoiding human studies and explains the unavailable NCI1 feature mapping. V2's explicit weak-structure performance limitation and caution about overtrusting extracted knowledge are removed.

D1.justification: V3 adds a LogicXGNN code-access link, specifies feature-free WL hashing and the 95% tree-accuracy criterion for selecting embedding dimensions, names the VF2 matching implementation, and provides CPU/memory running records. Baseline reproduction documentation substantially expands, including PGExplainer integration and supplying LogicXGNN-derived concepts to GLGExplainer. Several retained training and hardware details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 repositions the work around grounding failures and explanation faithfulness, adding relevant context from Laugel, Lipton, and Camburu. Related work expands to additional generative explainers and self-explainable GNNs, while chemistry-specific references supporting v2's discovery discussion disappear. This substantially changes research positioning beyond citation-format updates.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, research questions, evaluation narrative, related work, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. V2's single appendix with eleven subsections becomes separate dataset, setup, results, grounding, explanation, and LLM-usage appendices. This is substantial narrative and structural reorganization.

P2.justification: The framework overview is redrawn, and v3 adds a concept-versus-graph schematic, a depth-sensitivity plot, colored orbit-grounding diagrams, and ranked representative subgraphs. V2's generation panels and clause histograms disappear. Tables are substantially restructured around fidelity, scalability, utility, and expanded architecture comparisons, rather than merely renumbered or numerically updated.

improvement.justification: V3 addresses v2's accuracy-centered explanation evaluation with grounded fidelity, quantitative utility tests, and better reproduction documentation. However, Section 3.3 claims consistency across isomorphic subgraphs, while Theorem D.1 establishes fixed-instance determinism using node-ID tie breaks. Scalability reporting also conflicts: Twitch's Table 7 seed scores average 56.77%, versus 59.71% in Table 2. Alongside removal of scaffold-shift evidence and explicit limitations, these substantive gains and unresolved theoretical and reporting issues prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
